newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen moving narrowly, topside heavy.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen moving narrowly, topside heavy.

text.p: Japanese government bond (JGB) futures are expected to move narrowly around 124 during Tokyo trade on Thursday, with their topside weighted near 124.30 yen on investor profit-taking.
Sales of cash bonds by investors are also likely, particularly the 190-series, something that would undercut futures' strength somewhat, as happened on Wednesday.
But activity overall is expected to be inhibited ahead of the Denver G7 summit this weekend and the release of the Bank of Japan (BOJ)'s "tankan" quarterly survey of business sentiment next week.

"The market is likely to find it difficult to buy the benchmark futures contract much above 124.20 yen today, because to do so would make the coupon on next week's auction of 10-year bonds too low," one trust bank trader said.
Book-squaring sales were also likely following fairly quick rises earlier this week, he added.

The market will be watching moves in bank debentures after Wednesday's falls in response to a report in the Nihon Keizai Shimbun, later-denied, that the Finance Ministry's Trust Fund Bureau would stop buying bank debentures with funds from the government's Fiscal Investment and Loan Programme.
